items.title: Weather alert issued for southern Ontario including Mississauga, Brampton
items.summary: A weather alert has been issued for parts of southern Ontario on Thursday morning. Near-zero visibility in fog is expected, according to the alert from Environment and Climate Change Canada. The yellow-level advisory is in effect for Mississauga, Brampton, Caledon, Halton Hills, Burlington, Oakville, Newmarket, Georgina and northern York Region. m. Areas of dense fog will impact the area this morning, the alert states. Travel will likely be hazardous in some locations. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times. Drivers should be prepared for areas of near-zero visibility and allow extra time to reach their destinations, Environment Canada said. The fog is expected to dissipate in the morning.

items.title: Elliot Lake Drug Raid Nets Mississauga Man Among Two People Charged
items.summary: According to the Ontario Provincial Police, a Mississauga man is one of two people charged after officers executed a search warrant Tuesday night at an apartment in Elliot Lake, roughly 160 kilometres west of Sudbury. The OPP reports officers recovered a large quantity of hard drugs during the raid. According to police, the investigation involved the OPP's Community Street Crime Unit, Organized Crime Enforcement Bureau and the East Algoma detachment. The OPP identified the two people charged as 45-year-old Jennifer Stubbert of Elliot Lake and 20-year-old Kory Joseph-Labban of Mississauga. Police say both face numerous charges stemming from the drug seizure. According to the OPP, both were held in custody and scheduled to appear Wednesday in bail court at the Ontario Court of Justice in Blind River.

items.title: Halton police officer charged in 2025 pursuit that left one person injured: SIU
items.summary: A Halton regional police officer who was involved in a vehicle chase that left one person seriously injured in Mississauga last year has been charged. The logo of the Ontario Special Investigations Unit is pictured in Toronto, April 12, 2024. A Halton regional police officer who was involved in a vehicle chase that left one person seriously injured in Mississauga last year has been charged. Ontario’s police watchdog says it has reasonable grounds to lay a criminal charge against Sgt. David Joseph after the pursuit of a stolen vehicle that collided with a tractor trailer. The Special Investigations Unit says officers were investigating the theft of a Kia Sedona in Oakville that also involved a stolen GMC Hummer on March 12, 2025. The SIU says the drivers of both vehicles fled the area. It says a 26-year-old driver was seriously injured after the Hummer collided with a tractor trailer during the police pursuit led by Joseph in the area of Winston Churchill Boulevard and Lakeshore Road East in Mississauga. The watchdog says the officer has been charged with dangerous operation of a conveyance causing bodily harm and is scheduled to appear before a Milton court in November.

items.title: SIU Charges Halton Sergeant More Than a Year After Stolen-Hummer Crash on Mississauga Border
items.summary: According to Ontario's Special Investigations Unit, a Halton Regional Police sergeant has been charged more than a year after a chase involving a stolen Hummer ended in a crash at Winston Churchill Boulevard and Lakeshore Road East, on the Mississauga-Oakville border. The SIU reports Halton officers were investigating the theft of a Kia Sedona and a GMC Hummer from a home in Oakville when the drivers of both vehicles fled and officers pursued them through Oakville and Mississauga. According to the SIU, the chase was led by Sgt. David Joseph, and the Hummer's driver collided with a diesel fuel tractor-trailer. The SIU says the 26-year-old driver was arrested and taken to hospital with a serious injury. According to the SIU, Joseph has now been charged with dangerous operation of a conveyance causing bodily harm. The SIU reports Joseph is scheduled to appear in court in Milton on Nov. 23.

items.title: Naples-Trained Chef's Fermented-Dough Sandwiches Land at Square One's Food Court
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Vero Italian Sandwich Co. has opened a new location inside the food court at Square One Shopping Centre, bringing its oversized sandwiches to Mississauga. The outlet reports the Toronto chain was built around the vision of Chef Daniele Gagliotta, a world-champion pizza maker from Naples who brought his dough-making expertise to the sandwich business. Insauga.com says Vero builds its sandwiches on schiacciata, a traditional Italian flatbread, using dough that undergoes a 72-hour cold fermentation process and flour imported from Italy. According to the outlet, the sandwiches feature Italian deli meats, specialty cheeses and fresh toppings, including a signature sandwich called the Don Angelo with prosciutto, burrata, Parmigiano, tomato, balsamic glaze and arugula. The outlet reports the Square One shop is Vero's third location, following its original spot on Queen Street West in Toronto and a newer location at Upper Canada Mall in Newmarket. Insauga.com notes meats and cheeses are sliced to order as part of the shop's in-store experience.

items.title: Property Tax Freeze Would Go Permanent for Seniors Under Tedjo's Platform
items.summary: According to Now Toronto, newly elected Mississauga Mayor Alvin Tedjo has promised to freeze property taxes for all residents for two years, funded by cutting waste, a hiring freeze and avoiding new spending. The outlet reports Tedjo has pledged to make that freeze permanent for residents aged 65 and older, with specific eligibility rules to be worked out with city council. According to Now Toronto, Tedjo has also promised to raise the annual property tax rebate for low-income seniors from $571 to roughly $700 to account for inflation. The outlet reports Tedjo's campaign, which also promised to hire more police officers, centred on affordability, housing, public safety and traffic congestion. According to Now Toronto, Tedjo defeated incumbent Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie in the Oct. 26 election. The outlet reports Tedjo has said crime and public safety have become increasingly serious concerns for Mississauga residents.

items.title: After Years of Resident Pressure, Mississauga Will Again Clear Snow Piles From Every Driveway
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga's winter maintenance crews will once again clear windrows, the heavy piles of snow and ice left at the end of driveways after plows pass, from every residential driveway in the city this winter. The outlet reports the city first offered this driveway-clearing service last winter after residents pushed city council for years to address the problem. Helen Noehammer, the city's director of works operations and maintenance, told insauga.com the service was well received overall last winter. According to the outlet, Noehammer is reminding residents to help the program run smoothly by moving parked vehicles off the street whenever the city declares a winter parking restriction during heavy snowfall. The outlet reports vehicles left on the road, including in areas with new 15-hour parking rules this year, could be fined $150 or towed. Insauga.com notes the reminder comes as cold, snowy weather approaches in the coming weeks.

items.title: Mississauga's Cycling Advisory Committee Opens Nominations for Its Annual Advocacy Awards
items.summary: According to mississauga.com, the city's Cycling Advisory Committee is accepting nominations through Jan. 8 for its 2026 cycling advocacy awards. The outlet reports the awards recognize residents, local businesses and students who promoted cycling and active transportation across Mississauga throughout the year. Nominees must live in Mississauga and must not have won a committee award within the past four years, according to mississauga.com. The outlet reports current committee members, city and Peel Region employees who work in cycling or sustainable transportation, and their immediate family, are not eligible. According to mississauga.com, anyone nominating someone must submit a form along with two supporting letters, and self-nominations are also accepted. The outlet reports the committee will review nominations and announce recipients at a council meeting in spring 2027.
